title: The deaths at Carthage are presented as a sealing witness
setting: Joseph Smith and his brother Hyrum were shot by a mob at the jail in Carthage, Illinois, on 27 June 1844. John Taylor was wounded, and Willard Richards escaped unhurt. This statement was written soon after and placed at the end of the 1844 edition of the Doctrine and Covenants. That edition was nearly ready for printing in Nauvoo when the killings happened. The official heading names no author, but the statement is traditionally attributed to John Taylor.
summary: This is not a revelation but a written announcement and tribute, speaking as “we”. It reports that Joseph and Hyrum Smith were shot at Carthage Jail by a mob of 150 to 200 men. It records their last words and says John Taylor was wounded and Willard Richards escaped. It then praises Joseph Smith’s work, including the Book of Mormon and the revelations in this book. It quotes Joseph saying he went “like a lamb to the slaughter” with a clear conscience. It adds that Hyrum read a passage from Ether 12 before leaving for Carthage. It gives the brothers’ ages and calls them martyrs. It ends by saying their innocent blood, on Carthage jail, Illinois, and the nation, is a witness to the gospel. That blood will cry to the Lord until he avenges it.

contextNote.title: Why the statement calls their blood a seal
contextNote.text: Readers in 1844 had to make sense of a prophet killed in custody. Verse 3 frames the deaths as a seal: he “sealed his mission and his works with his own blood”. Verse 1 opens the same way, saying the announcement is made “to seal the testimony” of this book. Verse 5 supplies the legal image behind the word: “the testators are now dead, and their testament is in force”. Verse 7 then places that blood on Carthage jail, on Illinois for its broken pledge, and on the nation. In this passage, to seal means to confirm a testimony as final, the way a death puts a will into effect.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 135–136 presents Joseph and Hyrum Smith as faithful witnesses who sealed their testimony with their lives. What does verse 3 list as Joseph Smith’s work, and which part of that list matters most in your own faith?
reviewNote: Read all 7 verses. Official heading gives the 27 June 1844 date, Carthage Jail, the mob size, and inclusion at the end of the 1844 edition; it names no author. Attribution to John Taylor is traditional and stated as such. No JSP revelation document exists (written after Joseph Smith's death). dateLabel is approximate: written between late June and the edition's appearance later in 1844; month set to 1844-06 to sit beside the event on the timeline. receivedAt set to nauvoo, where the 1844 edition was being printed; exact place of writing is not stated in the heading. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary said the blood is “a witness against Illinois”; verse 7 calls it a witness “to the truth of the everlasting gospel,” with Illinois named for its broken pledge. Corrected. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote verse 7 sentence reworded to match what the verse says.
